items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: As I told you before, knowing and listening to Chick Webb play helped me to model some of my ideas.

ctx.x: know Sidney did, too. I admired and idolized his work, it was impeccable. You can't say enough or much more. He shaded his lows as the music demanded with such intense intuitiveness, it was almost uncanny. The drummer's drummer.

As I told you before, knowing and listening to Chick Webb play helped me to model some of my ideas. He tuned his drums. Sidney Catlett, too, about the same way, with opened and dampened heads, and got a high sound. Chick Webb's was predominantly on the soloist's side, and it was just so wonderful, you had to hear them. There weren't enough recordings of his, and of course, they were very technical -- I mean, they were full of technique, is what I should say, swinging technically.

And I adapted to tuning my drums along those lines, and still adhere to those sounds today. I can't stand a deep snare drum's tone. That's why I use a three and a half, or at the most, a four-inch deep snare. I like the four-inch by 13-inch in diameter, the so-called piccolo snare drum in my work -- I've been using it for a long time for a crisp sound.
